A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Zeroth-Order Optimization Finds Flat Minima. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on a synthetic function, binary classification, and RoBERTa fine-tuning, including optimization trajectories and runtime/memory measurements in Figures 1–6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their reported outcomes in Figures 1–6 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same Gaussian two-point estimator, parameter update, smoothing parameter, and output selection. No algorithmic component or training objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Example 2.1, SVMs and logistic regression on a5a and w5a, and RoBERTa-Large fine-tuning on SST-2, SST-5, and TREC. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain gradient descent and the same zeroth-order variants, including the limiting directional-derivative variant in the synthetic experiment. Newly cited SAM-inspired methods are discussed as related work, not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D retain the same data sampling, model size, full-batch training, iteration budgets, hyperparameters, and Hessian-trace estimation procedure. The new introductory sentence in Section 4 does not introduce an experiment or protocol.

E4.justification: The smoothing-parameter analysis in Figures 1 and 4 and the additional-seed experiments in Figures 4–6 are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix D reports the same random seeds and three-seed experiments. Table 2 retains the same practice of reporting mean runtime and standard error across seeds 42, 21, and 87.

E6.justification: Figures 1–6 contain identical plot images, and Table 2 retains all runtime, uncertainty, and memory values. The reported loss, Hessian-trace, accuracy, and comparative findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, convergence rates, and proofs are substantively unchanged. Remark 3.1 repeats differentiability already required by Assumption 3.3. Remark C.3 replaces the Lipschitz inequality with the equivalent bounded-gradient condition; differentiability was already implied by its retained higher-order smoothness assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claim of convergence of standard two-point zeroth-order optimization to flat minima under convexity and smoothness assumptions, with the same complexity guarantee and empirical support.

C2.justification: The interpretation of smoothing as implicit Hessian-trace regularization and the explanations of experimental behavior remain unchanged. The stated limitations concerning convexity, higher-order smoothness, and gradient-estimation variance are also retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly provides a FlatZero code-repository link at the beginning of Section 4. Appendix D's implementation settings, hardware, resource measurements, and data-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds SharpZO and Sharpness-aware black-box optimization to the existing LORENZA discussion. It explicitly distinguishes their SAM-inspired modifications from this paper's study of implicit regularization in standard zeroth-order optimization.

P1.justification: Localized edits expand the related-work paragraph, add an experiment-section introduction and code pointer, clarify smoothness wording, and update affiliation and acknowledgement text. The overall narrative and section structure are retained.

P2.justification: Added prose causes limited text reflow across pages 10–12 and bibliography pages 19–20. Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–2 retain their organization, captions, and visual content; no display is added or redesigned.

improvement.justification: The new code pointer improves reproducibility guidance, while the expanded related-work discussion more clearly distinguishes the contribution from SAM-inspired zeroth-order methods. These are useful, limited improvements; the scientific method, theoretical guarantees, experiments, and results remain unchanged.
